description: How a phone applies what comes back from the server (Android and iOS). Given its local state (feed position `after`, entities with their known server versions, the queue, open conflicts) and one step (a changes page, the receipts for the queue's sent commands, or the user resolving a conflict), the local state afterwards and any notices for the user. Page: a delete removes the entity and cleans up exactly as a `gone` receipt does, even when the entity has queued commands or an open conflict: its unsent commands are dropped (sent ones wait for their receipts) and its conflict is closed; a delete of something the phone doesn't have is ignored. Any other change to an entity with a queued command or an open conflict updates only its known version (and the conflict's server copy); otherwise an active change is stored (unless older than the known version); then after = next_after. The page is applied in one transaction. Receipts, matched in order to the sent commands, each remove its command: applied records the version and closes any conflict, and applies each `cascaded` entry (a user_tag or custom_dhikr delete's cascades) to an entity the phone has as a page change would: an active one sets its known version unless older, a deleted one removes it; duplicate acts as its original; conflict keeps the local document, drops later unsent commands for the entity and opens a conflict; merged moves every local use of the tag ID to the surviving tag; gone removes the entity; rejected restores the server's copy (or removes the entity when there is none) and adds a notice, except for a custom_dhikr put rejected with audio_not_found or audio_mismatch, which loses nothing: the phone keeps its local document, with audio {"local_only": true} and the recording queued for upload again if its file is still on the phone (local_audio_files), or audio null otherwise; its known version becomes the server's (0 when current is null); the entity's unsent commands are replaced by one put of that document on that version, queued where the first unsent command was (or, if the phone has deleted the entity since, a delete on the server's version, or nothing when the server has none); and a notice with the code is added. New commands take new_command_ids in order. Removing a custom dhikr, by a page or a receipt, removes its dhikr_personal and that record's unsent commands; removing a tag removes it from local dhikr_personal documents and unsent commands. Resolve keep_mine queues the local version (or delete) on the server's version; use_theirs takes the server's copy.

entities.description: Entities present on the phone (deleted ones are gone), sorted by entity_type, then entity_id. known_version is the last server version seen; 0 if the server hasn't confirmed it yet.

conflicts.description: Open conflicts, sorted by entity_type, then entity_id. local_op is put if the entity exists locally, else delete.

new_command_ids.description: IDs for the commands this step queues, used in order (UUIDv7s the phone would generate).

command_id.description: The new command's ID for keep_mine; null for use_theirs.

local_audio_files.description: Custom dhikr IDs whose imported recording file is still in the profile's files (slice 3c). It only matters for an audio_not_found or audio_mismatch rejection.

cases.description: Changes without local edits are applied as they come: an update replaces the document and known version, a new entity is added, and after moves to next_after.

translation.en: Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him.

translation.en: Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him.

cases.description: A delete removes the entity; the server sends the cascaded dhikr_personal delete as its own change.
A delete of something this phone never had is ignored.
A delete removes the entity even with unsent commands queued for it: they're dropped, as a gone receipt drops them, and so are its dhikr_personal and that record's unsent command.
A deleted custom dhikr's dhikr_personal goes with it even when the server never had that record (so no delete arrives for it): the record and its unsent create are dropped.

A deleted tag is removed locally from every dhikr_personal and unsent command, including a record the server doesn't have yet (no cascade arrives for it); records the server did change arrive as changes at the same revision.
A delete of an entity with an open conflict removes it and closes the conflict: there's nothing left to keep or take.
A new profile reads from after=0 and stores everything it gets.
A change to an entity with a queued local edit updates only its known version. The local document and the queued command (still on version 3) stay; the conflict surfaces when it's sent.
A change to an entity deleted locally but not yet sent doesn't bring it back.
The phone's own applied change comes back in the feed with the server's document, which wins: here the server rewrote a merged tag ID.
A change older than the version this phone already knows is ignored.
A change to an entity with an open conflict refreshes the conflict's server copy and the known version; the local document stays.

translation.en: Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him.

cases.description: applied: the command leaves the queue and the entity's known version becomes the receipt's.
A later unsent command for the same entity stays queued; it was already chained on the version this receipt confirms.

A tag delete was saved locally (the tag taken out of both records, with no dhikr_personal put queued) and sent. Its applied receipt lists the records the server changed at the same revision; their known versions move to those at once, so the next edit of either is made on the right version.
A custom dhikr delete's receipt lists its deleted dhikr_personal. The phone removed that record when it saved the delete, so the entry finds nothing to change.
duplicate is handled as its original receipt (here a resend after a lost response).
conflict: the local edit stays, an open conflict records the server's copy for Keep mine / Use theirs, and later unsent commands for the entity are dropped (the local document already holds them).

translation.en: Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him.

cases.description: A local delete that conflicts records local_op delete; the entity stays deleted locally until the user chooses.
merged into a tag this phone hasn't pulled yet: the local tag takes the surviving ID, name and version, and every local use of the old ID (dhikr_personal documents and unsent commands) is rewritten.
merged into a tag this phone already has: the duplicate local tag goes, its uses are rewritten without repeats, and unsent commands for the merged tag are dropped.
gone: the entity was deleted elsewhere. It's removed locally with its unsent commands, and a custom dhikr's dhikr_personal goes with it.
rejected: the entity goes back to the server's copy and the user is told (a notice with the code).
A rejected create has no server copy, so the entity is removed; a removed tag is also taken out of local dhikr_personal documents and unsent commands.

An audio_not_found rejection (here the asset was cleaned up while the put waited in the queue) loses nothing: the local edit stays, its audio goes back to {"local_only": true}, the recording is queued for upload again because its file is still on the phone, a put of the edit is queued so the text syncs now, and the user is told. The upload names a new asset and queues its own put once confirmed.

A rejected create isn't removed when the reason is its audio: with the recording's file no longer on the phone, audio becomes null and the create is queued again on version 0, ahead of the unsent personal record that needs it, so no tag is lost either.

audio_mismatch is handled the same way. The entity's unsent follow-up, chained on a version the rejected put never made, is replaced by one put of the latest local document on the server's version; the recording is queued for upload again.
If the user deleted the dhikr after the rejected put, nothing comes back: its unsent delete is replaced by a delete on the server's version, so the server copy goes as the user meant.
Receipts match the sent commands one to one, in order; unsent commands wait for the next batch.
Keep mine: the local document is queued again on the server's version.

cases.description: Use theirs: the server's copy replaces the local edit and nothing is queued.
